company_items.summary: Citigroup posted a strong Q3 beat with EPS of $2.85, up 27% and well above the Street's $2.65 estimate, on revenue of $23.85B (+8%) versus expectations of $23.72B. The efficiency ratio improved 290 basis points to 59%, provisions came in slightly below estimates at $2.58B, and IB fees rose 9% with Equity Underwriting surging 77% year-over-year. Full-year guidance was nudged higher on both net interest income (now mid-to-high 6% sales growth vs. prior 5-6%) and ROTCE (now 11% vs. prior 10-11%).

sectors: Large-cap bank earnings showing strength in FICC, equities underwriting, and expense discipline, with improved return on tangible common equity guidance signaling confidence in the back half of the year.
tts_summary: Let's wrap up the morning earnings slate with Citigroup, and it's a clean beat across the board. The bank reported third-quarter earnings per share of two dollars and eighty-five cents, up twenty-seven percent year-over-year and a solid twenty cents ahead of the Street's two-sixty-five estimate. Revenue came in at twenty-three point eight five billion, up eight percent and just above consensus at twenty-three point seven two billion. The real story here is execution — the efficiency ratio improved two hundred and ninety basis points to fifty-nine percent, beating the Street's sixty point seven percent estimate, meaning management is squeezing more out of every dollar of revenue. Provisions were also slightly favorable at two point five eight billion versus the expected two point six five billion, and they only built three hundred and sixty-nine million in reserves, which signals they're not seeing meaningful credit deterioration. Inside the investment bank, fixed income currencies and commodities revenue rose four percent to four point three eight billion, beating estimates of four point two six billion. Equities revenue climbed fourteen percent to one point seven two billion, slightly shy of the one point seven seven billion the Street had penciled in — so a minor miss there, but not meaningful in the context of the overall beat. IB fees were a bright spot, up nine percent to one point three five billion versus one point two six billion expected, and equity underwriting surged seventy-seven percent year-over-year, which speaks to the broader pickup in capital markets activity. On guidance, management nudged the full-year outlook higher in two key areas. Net interest income is now tracking toward mid-to-high six percent sales growth for the full year, up from the prior five to six percent range. Return on tangible common equity guidance was also raised to eleven percent from a prior range of ten to eleven percent — a subtle but meaningful tightening to the upside. Bottom line: this is a strong print from Citigroup. Expense control is improving, capital markets are recovering, credit quality is holding, and management is confident enough to raise the bar on profitability targets. For the broader financial sector, this continues the theme of large banks delivering better-than-feared results this earnings season.
